newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Asahi Bank, fined in US, cleans up branch.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Asahi Bank, fined in US, cleans up branch.

text.p: Japan's Asahi Bank, fined in the United States for misconduct at its New York branch, said on Friday it had reshuffled senior management at the branch and formulated steps to improve operations there.

In the second recent case involving U.S. branches of top Japanese banks, the U.S. Federal Reserve on Thursday fined Asahi and its New York branch a total of $5 million for misuse of confidential supervisory information.
Senior officials in the branch also made false statements to bank supervisory officials, the Fed said.

Asahi did not admit any of the Fed's charges but signed an agreement to abide by the orders and agreed to train all its U.S.-based personnel "in ethics and the United States bank supervisory process", the Fed said.

The training was to emphasise "the necessity for candor in all communications with bank supervisors, especially during bank examinations", as well as possible sanctions for failing to comply with the law.
In a statement issued on Friday, Asahi said it found through its own investigation that several employees of the New York branch had used inspection materials left by U.S. regulators at the branch.
The internal investigation also found that the employees initially denied their involvement, the bank said.
Asahi said in the statement that senior management of the New York branch had been reshuffled and workers involved in the case removed from their positions at that time.

Thursday"s announcement by the Fed came just a year after another major Japanese bank, Daiwa Bank Ltd, pleaded guilty to 16 charges that it covered up a $1.1 billion loss in unauthorised trading at its New York branch.
Daiwa was fined a record $340 million by U.S. authorities.

A tell-all book by the former Daiwa bond trader who was sent to prison for the scandal said regulators in Japan and the U.S. were careless in not detecting his wrongdoings, and also said Daiwa tried to cover up the losses.
Daiwa Bank and Japan's Ministry of Finance have both declined comment on the book, which was published last month.
The trading scandal forced the bank to shut down its U.S. operations and sparked criticism of the ministry"s handling of the affair.
An Asahi official said on Friday that the bank would maintain its U.S. operations despite being fined.
The Finance Ministry, meanwhile, said it would take appropriate measures against Asahi, but stopped short of saying what those steps might be.
"We will take some kind of measure (against Asahi Bank) as it failed to comply with foreign authorities," a ministry official said.
Asahi shares dipped in Tokyo following the news but were spared a sell-off in a market enjoying a recovery led by active buying of blue chips.
The bank's shares ended the session down just one yen at 812 yen with 2.32 million shares traded. ($1=124 yen)
